# EX-COMP-011 — Context Reliability Reversal

## Objective

Test whether context congruency helps perception primarily when sensory evidence is weak
and offers less benefit—or reverses—when evidence is clear.

## Design

Present expected and unexpected interface elements under low-contrast and high-contrast
conditions. Cross context congruency, signal reliability, target location, and task.

## Measures

- identification accuracy
- reaction time
- time to first fixation
- confidence and confidence calibration

## Prediction

Congruency improves performance under weak evidence but provides less benefit or an
unexpected-target advantage under clear evidence.

## Falsification Condition

Context congruency produces the same benefit at every signal-reliability level.

## Analysis Requirement

Separate perceptual sensitivity from decision criterion where possible; gaze, reaction
time, and confidence alone cannot establish a changed perceptual representation.
